name: First Day at a New Job
blurb: A POV first day: five office types, one actor, and a twist that explains everything
title: First Day at a New Job: 60-Second POV Comedy Script
description: A 60-second POV comedy script for 1 or 2 performers: a new hire meets five office types, all played by one actor, with a twist. Free to film.
h1: First Day at a New Job: a 60-Second POV Comedy Script
logline: The camera is the new hire, and every coworker on day one is a type you already know. The strange part: they all look exactly alike, and nobody seems to notice.
setting: Any desk, a doorway and a fridge, in daytime. Props: a lanyard, glasses, a cardigan, a headset, a tie or scarf, a sticky note, a packet of biscuits.

roles.name: New hire
roles.note: Any gender, 18+. The camera. Nervous, friendly, just wants to find their desk.

roles.name: Coworker
roles.note: Any gender, 18+. One performer plays all five coworkers, each with one costume piece.

script.text: ON SCREEN: POV: your first day

script.action: POV. A smiling MANAGER in a lanyard waves at the camera.

script.say: Welcome! We're like a family here.

script.text: ON SCREEN: The one who says family

script.action: Cut. A DESK NEIGHBOUR in glasses spins round. Same actor.

script.say: Quick question. Do you know spreadsheets? Great. You're me now.

script.action: Cut. An IT PERSON in a headset. Same actor.

script.say: Your password needs eight letters, a number and one tear.

script.action: Cut. A hand reaches into the fridge. A SNACK GUARD in a cardigan blocks it.

script.say: Those biscuits are labelled. Read the label.

script.action: Close-up of the sticky note: NOT YOURS.
Cut. A MEETING LOVER in a tie.

script.say: Let's book a meeting. To plan the meeting.

script.text: ON SCREEN: Books meetings for fun

script.say: Sorry. Are you all the same person?

script.action: The camera pans. All five coworkers stand in a row. Same face.

script.say: We told you. We're a family here.

script.text: ON SCREEN: Tomorrow: meet Mum, the CEO

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 holding the phone at eye height so it feels like the new hire's eyes; let one hand come into frame now and then. The coworker performer changes one costume piece per character and speaks straight into the lens. For the line-up, put the phone on a tripod, mark five spots on the floor and film the actor in each costume on each spot, then split-screen or cut them together in any editing app. Daylight from a window is best. Two takes per coworker is plenty.

ul: Give each coworker one strong physical habit: the manager's double thumbs-up, the desk neighbour's spin, the snack guard's folded arms.
Talk to the lens, not beside it. In POV, the lens is the new hire's face.
The new hire's lines should sound tired and polite, more so each time.
Leave a short silence before the siblings line so viewers can notice the faces first.
Common mistake: changing your voice too much. Keep the same voice and let the costume do the work; it makes the twist land.
Set it on the first day at a new school: the strict teacher, the class clown, the canteen guard, the group-chat admin.
With two performers, the new hire appears on camera and reacts in a mirror or window reflection.
Part-two hook: day two, Mum the CEO arrives, and she is played by the new hire.

prompts.keyframe: First-person point of view in a bright open-plan office, a smiling coworker with a lanyard reaches toward the camera to shake hands, the viewer's hand visible at frame edge, soft daylight, cinematic still, vertical 9:16.
shots: First-person handheld shot walking into a bright office, a smiling manager in a lanyard greets the camera warmly, light comedy mood, soft daylight, vertical 9:16.
First-person shot, a hand reaches into an office fridge for biscuits, a coworker in a cardigan steps in and blocks it with folded arms, close-up on a sticky note, comic tension, vertical 9:16.
Slow pan across five coworkers standing in a row in an office, all with the same face but different glasses, ties and cardigans, they smile at the camera together, surreal comedy, vertical 9:16.

faq.q: How does one person play all five coworkers?
faq.a: Film each coworker separately with a different costume piece, then cut between them. For the line-up, keep the phone on a tripod, film the same spot five times and combine the clips with a split-screen or mask tool in your editing app.

faq.q: Can I add my own office types?
faq.a: Yes. Keep one line and one caption per type, and swap in your own: the loud phone talker, the plant parent, the one who replies to all. Keep it under a minute by removing one type for each one you add.

faq.q: Can I post it on a brand or company account?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0, including commercial use. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the caption.
